nodes.name: Inertial frame
nodes.statement: An inertial frame is a frame of reference in which a free object moves in a straight line at constant speed.

nodes.name: Principle of relativity
nodes.statement: The laws of physics take the same form in every inertial frame. No experiment inside a closed, uniformly moving lab can detect its motion.

nodes.name: Maxwell predicts c
nodes.statement: Maxwell's equations predict electromagnetic waves moving at c = 1/√(μ₀ε₀), and the equations name no frame that this speed is measured against.

nodes.name: Michelson-Morley result
nodes.statement: The Michelson-Morley experiment of 1887 found no change in the speed of light as the Earth moved in different directions through space.

nodes.name: Constant speed of light
nodes.statement: Light in vacuum moves at c ≈ 299,792 km/s in every inertial frame, whatever the motion of its source.

nodes.name: Relativity of simultaneity
nodes.statement: Two distant events that are simultaneous in one frame are not simultaneous in a frame moving along the line between them.

nodes.name: Light clock
nodes.statement: A light clock ticks each time a pulse bounces between two mirrors. In a frame where the clock moves sideways, the pulse follows a longer diagonal path at the same speed c.

nodes.name: Lorentz factor
nodes.statement: The Lorentz factor is γ = 1/√(1 − v²/c²). It equals 1 at rest and grows without bound as v approaches c.

nodes.name: Time dilation
nodes.statement: A moving clock runs slow by the factor γ. A time Δτ on the clock is measured as Δt = γΔτ in a frame where the clock moves.

nodes.name: Length contraction
nodes.statement: An object moving at speed v is shortened along its direction of motion to L = L₀/γ, where L₀ is its length at rest.

nodes.name: Muons reach the ground
nodes.statement: Muons made high in the atmosphere live only about 2.2 μs at rest, yet many reach the ground. Time dilation stretches their lifetime in the Earth's frame.

nodes.name: The muon's view
nodes.statement: In the muon's own frame its lifetime is normal. It reaches the ground because the atmosphere is contracted to a small fraction of its rest thickness.

nodes.name: Lorentz transformation
nodes.statement: Coordinates in two frames with relative speed v are related by x′ = γ(x − vt) and t′ = γ(t − vx/c²).

nodes.name: Velocity addition
nodes.statement: Velocities combine as w = (u + v)/(1 + uv/c²). Combining any two speeds below c always gives a speed below c.

nodes.name: Spacetime interval
nodes.statement: The interval s² = c²Δt² − Δx² − Δy² − Δz² between two events has the same value in every inertial frame.

nodes.name: Proper time
nodes.statement: Proper time is the time shown by a clock carried along a path. For a straight path at constant speed it equals s/c, where s² is the interval.

nodes.name: Light cone
nodes.statement: The light cone of an event splits spacetime into its future, its past, and a region that can neither affect it nor be affected by it.

nodes.name: Causal order is absolute
nodes.statement: When one event can send a signal at or below c to another, every inertial observer agrees on which came first.

nodes.name: Twins are not symmetric
nodes.statement: The two twins are not equivalent, because only the travelling twin changes inertial frame when turning around.

nodes.name: Twin paradox
nodes.statement: A twin who travels away and returns is younger than the twin who stayed home. The traveller's path through spacetime has less proper time.

nodes.name: Relativistic momentum
nodes.statement: The momentum that is conserved in every frame is p = γmv, which grows without bound as v approaches c.

nodes.name: Energy-momentum relation
nodes.statement: Total energy satisfies E² = (pc)² + (mc²)². For a body moving at speed v this equals E = γmc².

nodes.name: Rest energy
nodes.statement: A body at rest has energy E = mc². One gram of mass corresponds to about 9 × 10¹³ joules.

nodes.name: Light speed is a limit
nodes.statement: No object with mass can be accelerated to c, because its energy γmc² would become infinite.

nodes.name: Massless particles
nodes.statement: A particle with zero mass, such as a photon, has E = pc and always travels at exactly c.

nodes.name: Binding lowers mass
nodes.statement: A nucleus has less mass than its separate protons and neutrons. The missing mass times c² is the energy released when the nucleus forms.

nodes.name: GPS clock correction
nodes.statement: GPS satellite clocks fall behind by about 7 μs per day because of their orbital speed. Engineers correct for this together with a larger gain of about 45 μs per day from weaker gravity.
